advances: The caps are an actual cover and source-active for the one-cap residual problem. They are not asserted to be a critical deepest-point cover or to meet a subtarget mixed cap budget. The witness refutes the unconditional root-to-volume step only.

proof:
The determinant of the vertex vectors is $q!$, so $|T|=1$ and for $0<s<2$ the part of $2T$ with $\ell(x)<s$ has volume $s^q$ by similarity. The lesser of the two upper thresholds is $1-a|z|\le1$, so the two upper caps and the lower cap cover the entire real body; every trace at a sampled base is proper. The residual roots there are $1+az$, $1-az$, and $(2^q-1)^{1/q}>1$. Their minimum is as stated. Every feasible nonnegative sampled convex majorant satisfies $h_0\ge1$ and $h_{-1}+h_1\ge2h_0$. Thus by strict convexity $\sum_z h_z^q\ge3h_0^q\ge3$, with equality only at the feasible constant $h=1$.

Use the supporting inequalities $h_i+g_i(z_j-z_i)-h_j\le0$ and obstacles $e_i-h_i\le0$ with multipliers $
u_{ij}$ and $\lambda_i$, respectively. Put $g_i=0$, $
u_{0,-1}=
u_{0,1}=q$, $\lambda_0=3q$, and all other multipliers zero. The slope stationarity sum $\sum_j
u_{ij}(z_j-z_i)$ is zero in each row. Height stationarity is $q-\lambda_i+\sum_j
u_{ij}-\sum_j
u_{ji}=0$: at the center this is $q-3q+2q=0$ and at each endpoint $q-q=0$. Complementarity holds because the supporting inequalities are tight and the only positive obstacle multiplier is at the contact $0$. The martingale with entries $\pi_{0,-1}=\pi_{0,0}=\pi_{0,1}=q$ and others zero has source marginal $\lambda$, target marginal $(q,q,q)$, source mean zero, and constant threshold one. This is the two outgoing transfers together with the center's retained mass. It is a row of the original optimization, not a row postulated independently of it.

At the source $H_+$ attains the best one-cap residual root. The similarity formula gives exactly $(1-a,1,1+a)$ on its three strict residual traces. The ordinary roots average to one, but strict convexity gives $\Delta_q(a)>0$. All original fibers are identical, so their Brunn–Minkowski comparisons have zero slack. Subtract the displayed residual volumes from $2^q$ at every fiber for the captured averages and cap masses; the lower cap has one unit of volume in every fiber. For $q=2$, $a=1/2$, the residual-volume average is $7/6$, the captured average is $17/6$ versus $3$ at the source, each upper cap mass is $17/2$, and the total mixed mass is $12$.

statement:
For an integer $q\ge2$ and $0<a<1$, put $T=\operatorname{conv}\lbrace0,e_1,\ldots,e_{q-1},q!e_q\rbrace$ and $\ell(x)=\sum_{k<q}x_k+x_q/q!$. The three closed caps $H_\pm=\lbrace\ell(x)\ge1\pm az\rbrace$ and $H_0=\lbrace\ell(x)\le1\rbrace$ cover $C=[-1,1]\times2T$. Use the sum of $q$-volumes over its complete integer base $\lbrace-1,0,1\rbrace$. The least one-cap residual roots are $(1-a,1,1-a)$. The unique optimal sampled convex threshold minimizing the sum of $q$th powers is $(1,1,1)$ of cost $3$. Its supporting-slope KKT system admits a source row at $0$ with equal probability $1/3$ to each base, all on its positive affine face.

The source-active cap $H_+$ has actual residual roots $(1-a,1,1+a)$ in this row, with mean $1$ and mean residual volume $1+\Delta_q(a)/3$, where $\Delta_q(a)=(1-a)^q+(1+a)^q-2>0$. The captured volume at the source is $2^q-1$ while its row average for the same cap is $2^q-1-\Delta_q(a)/3$. The actual mixed masses are $\mu(H_+)=\mu(H_-)=3(2^q-1)-\Delta_q(a)$, $\mu(H_0)=3$, and $\mu(C)=3\cdot2^q$.
title: An actual positive KKT row can increase residual volume at equal mean root
